title: Nuevo Trato Copper Law Passed
reason: Independent (non-Wikipedia) sourcing confirms Chile enacted the "Nuevo Trato del Cobre" (New Deal copper law) in 1955 under President Carlos Ibáñez del Campo (Law 11,828, May 5, 1955), which reduced/restructured effective tax rates and offered commercial, accounting and exchange-control benefits to the major foreign copper producers to stimulate investment and production. A separate independent search confirms Anaconda owned Chuquicamata and El Salvador, and Kennecott owned El Teniente — the two companies named in the event description as the intended beneficiaries — and that 1955 is used as the baseline year for measuring their subsequent investment/profit performance under this regime, consistent with the law's 1955 enactment. The description's framing (tax incentives to Anaconda/Kennecott in exchange for production/investment increases, and the law fueling nationalist debate over foreign ownership of copper, later culminating in "Chileanization" and full nationalization) matches the historical record found. One minor caveat: EBSCO's account emphasizes the law failed to attract the hoped-for increase in investment from the companies, so "increased copper output" is a modest overstatement of otherwise-disappointing investment results, but this is not material enough to change the year/country/core-mechanism match, so I rate this TRUE rather than PARTIAL.

title: Allende Accelerates Agrarian Reform and Urban Land Redistribution
reason: Independent sources confirm both halves of the event. (1) Agrarian acceleration: a declassified CIA Intelligence Memorandum (hosted on Wikisource, a domain distinct from the off-limits wikipedia.org) gives hard numbers: Allende's government expropriated 3,281 farms totaling 13.0 million acres (25% of farmland, 34% of irrigated land) between Nov 1970 and Sept 1972, versus 1,408 farms / 8.8 million acres (19%/25%) expropriated by Frei over his full six-year term (Nov 1964-Nov 1970) — explicitly noting 'the pace of expropriation speeded up markedly' and that Allende targeted the most productive farms. NACLA (nacla.org, independent) corroborates: 'During Allende's first two years, nearly all the remaining large estates were expropriated.' Other reporting puts cumulative Allende redistribution at ~2.4M hectares by end of 1971 alone (vs Frei's 3.5M-ha six-year total), and academic work (Bellisario, Journal of Agrarian Change/Wiley) confirms expropriated fundos were converted into asentamientos/cooperatives, with a shift to CERA state-farm structures 'from mid-1971 onward.' The precise 'more than the entire Frei period' threshold, by strict calendar-year-end-1971 hectare counts, appears to be reached slightly after 1971 (by ~18-22 months in), which is a minor timing nuance rather than a substantive error — the 'dramatic acceleration' and rough parity/surpassing of Frei's whole-term total within Allende's first year(s) is solidly supported. (2) Urban land occupations: an independent academic source (redalyc.org, Chilean sociology journal, not wikipedia.org) confirms that under Unidad Popular, urban 'tomas de terrenos' were state-supported — 'at least 344 successful urban land takeovers were registered in Santiago' between 1970-1973, with the government creating a National Office of Settlers and a Unified Central of Poblador to formalize support, and pobladores 'granted a protagonist role' — matching the description's claim of organized mass land occupations with tacit government support. Both the rural and urban components of the event are corroborated by non-Wikipedia sources with concrete figures; only the exact 'exceeds Frei's whole term' magnitude for 1971 specifically has minor imprecision.

title: Boric Announces Lithium Nationalization Strategy
reason: Multiple independent, non-Wikipedia sources confirm this materially as described. On April 20-21, 2023, Chilean President Gabriel Boric announced a National Lithium Strategy calling for majority state control (via CODELCO and ENAMI) of future lithium projects on Chile's salt flats, home to the world's largest lithium reserves, while honoring existing contracts (CNBC, Forbes, Foreign Policy, Mining.com, Mining-technology). The announcement was explicitly likened to Allende's 1971 copper nationalization (Common Dreams, Qz, Electrek reporting Boric invoked the Allende model) and drew strong business/investor pushback (Forbes, CGEP Columbia). Subsequently, Codelco and SQM reached a framework/final agreement (Dec 2023 framework, finalized May 2024) in which SQM extended its operating rights in the Salar de Atacama to 2060 in exchange for Codelco taking a majority (50%+1) stake — squarely matching "extending mining rights in exchange for increased state participation" (SQM.com, Bloomberg, Mining Weekly). Albemarle separately signed a contract modification ("Annex 2024," April 26, 2024) with the Chilean state resolving a dispute and adjusting its exploitation terms (AmericaEconomia/SEC filings) — a related but softer parallel than the SQM deal; this is a minor supporting-detail nuance, not a core year/country/actor discrepancy. Core facts (country, year, president, agencies, comparison, opposition) are all corroborated by independent sources.
